subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent tool-capable memory-flush agent turn before explicit, daily, and idle resets, and what blocking/background/config/security boundaries should govern it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior changes reset latency, silent tool execution, memory retention, plugin boundaries, and security expectations, so automation should not choose the permanent policy.

options.title: Define bounded pre-reset flush
options.body: Approve an explicit reset-memory policy with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, and sandbox constraints, then implement the selected path.

options.title: Keep reset persistence mechanical
options.body: Treat hook/session-memory improvements such as #61675 as the supported reset boundary and narrow or close this issue away from silent agent execution.

options.title: Defer to memory plugins
options.body: Require memory plugins or external memory services to own continuous persistence and only extend core events where current plugin APIs are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Define bounded pre-reset flush
recommendation.body: Approve an explicit reset-memory policy with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, and sandbox constraints, then implement the selected path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both the existing pre-compaction flush primitive and earlier reset handling, making them the best available owner for this cross-boundary behavior choice.
